topic: Witnessing the Stellar Career of Prof Tom Edgar
title: Witnessing the Stellar Career of Prof Tom Edgar
session_title: 10: In Honor of Tom Edgar’s 80th Birthday
abstract: Professor Edgar’s and my academic careers started within a year of each other and continued at the same academic institutions at which we started over our careers – an uncommon practice in present day academia. The large State institutions in which our professional lives were embedded offered many diverse opportunities through which to contribute. Prof Edgar did so in an exemplary fashion – I could only try to keep up! Although the scope of our technical activities extended broadly over process systems engineering, we did overlap but not extensively. However, our professional activities have crossed and recrossed paths at various points in time and within the context of various organizations (AIChE, CACHE, CCR). In this presentation I will recap some these points of convergence as they exemplify the impact that Prof Edgar has had on our profession and in addition were very valuable for me personally. He is indeed a rarity – a leader in all spheres of academic life teaching, research, leadership / service but, above all, he is a valued colleague.

topic: Contributions By Tom Edgar to Education and Teaching in Process Systems Engineering
title: Contributions By Tom Edgar to Education and Teaching in Process Systems Engineering
session_title: 10: In Honor of Tom Edgar’s 80th Birthday
abstract: In this presentation we highlight the outstanding contributions that Tom Edgar has made in terms of his pioneering textbooks in optimization and process dynamics and control. We also highlight his leadership in establishing and promoting the Computer Aids for Chemical Engineering Education (CACHE) program, as well as other educational initiatives Finally, we also highlight the impact that he has had as an academic professor and as a university administrator.

topic: Tom Edgar: Teacher, Department Chair, Research Colleague, Friend
title: Tom Edgar: Teacher, Department Chair, Research Colleague, Friend
session_title: 10: In Honor of Tom Edgar’s 80th Birthday
abstract: In this talk, I draw upon my experiences first as an undergraduate student in the chemical engineering department at the University of Texas taking classes from Tom Edgar and working as an undergraduate in his research group. From there I returned to the department as an assistant professor with Tom as my department chair. Together we started an industrial research consortium that is still in operation today. From these many personal and professional experiences over many years, I will illustrate how Tom influenced me and my career in profound ways.

topic: Advancing Manufacturing Sustainability Research: A Domain-Specific Large Language Model Perspective
title: Advancing Manufacturing Sustainability Research: A Domain-Specific Large Language Model Perspective
session_title: 10: In Honor of Tom Edgar’s 80th Birthday
abstract: Advancing research in manufacturing sustainability requires the development of more comprehensive and broadly applicable sustainability metrics, enhanced assessment methods, and robust decision-making tools capable of functioning under uncertainty. These innovations must be built upon thorough reviews of existing methodologies, technologies, tools, and well-documented industrial case studies. This is a particularly complex task, as some critical data and knowledge are publicly accessible, while others remain confidential or restricted. One promising solution to this challenge is the use of large language models (LLMs). However, general-purpose LLMs may lack the depth required for highly specialized industrial applications, domain-specific LLMs are often necessary. These models should be effective tools for helping pursue manufacturing sustainability, by enabling smarter, faster, and enhanced sustainability assessment, system analysis, informed decision-making, and effective communication tailored to sustainability contexts. Specifically, fine-tuned domain-specific LLMs can compare and recommend sustainability indicators, identify the minimum set of system parameters required for evaluating those indicators, and suggest the most appropriate assessment methodologies. If the dynamic sustainability is aimed, real-time monitoring is essential. In this context, domain-specific LLMs can extract and summarize relevant performance data from production logs, reports, and Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) systems, facilitating continuous improvement. In this paper, we present a general framework for developing domain-specific LLMs tailored to manufacturing sustainability. A case study is also provided to illustrate the potential benefits of this approach for advancing research in sustainable manufacturing.
